all_solved_problems.title: Coin Change

bfs.notes: Strong. Level-order, multi-source BFS, matrix BFS, right-side view, topological sort all covered. Course Schedule extends BFS to DAG cycle detection. Number of Islands re-drilled 2026-05-21. Rotting Oranges 2026-05-22 — multi-source BFS + level = minute pattern + if-queue minute guard + grid mutation as visited marker locked in. 6 bugs caught and documented.
aha_moments: Snapshot len(queue) before level loop — freezes the current floor boundary
Multi-source BFS from all '0' cells simultaneously
deque([root]) not deque(root) — deque takes iterable, TreeNode is not iterable
Right Side View = result.append(level[-1]) — same BFS template, just grab last element
Topological Sort cycle detection: processed count < numCourses means a cycle blocked remaining nodes
Matrix BFS does NOT pre-load a start node — scan first, trigger BFS only when unvisited '1' found. Each BFS call exhausts exactly one island.
Grid mutation trick: set grid[r][c]='0' when visited — eliminates the visited set entirely. Requires grid mutation permission confirmed in Step 1.
Rotting Oranges: 'if queue: minute += 1' — only count a minute if spreading actually happened. Without this, terminal BFS levels over-count by 1.
Queue empty != all fresh rotted. Queue empty means BFS finished. Isolated fresh oranges are never touched. Only fresh_count == 0 confirms all rotted.
Grid mutation trick applies to Rotting Oranges too: mark grid[r][c]=2 when rotted — eliminates visited set entirely.

Clone Graph: hashmap[node] = clone BEFORE for-loop — this is what prevents infinite cycles.
hashmap[node] in the if-branch append refers to CURRENT stack frame's node, not the neighbor. Classic confusion point.
Deep copy = every node is a new object independent of original. Shallow copy = neighbors still point to original nodes.
